defect.evidence_quote:
The plain view doctrine authorizes a warrantless seizure of evidence

when (1) the police must observe the object from a lawful vantage point; (2)

the incriminating character of the object must be immediately apparent10; and

(3) the police must have a lawful right of access to the object.

defect.proposed_fix: Replace pin-26 with the actual slip-op. 26 plain-view-test passage and note any omitted footnote marker after 'immediately apparent'.

reasons: The disclosed lake pinpoint for pin-26 stores unrelated content-page prose beginning '— which became the basis for charges' rather than the opinion passage cited at slip op. 26.

residual_risks: The displayed content quote is substantively present in the opinion, but the stored pin-26 quote under review is not character-faithful.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Use the actual opinion text for the pin and avoid harvesting page prose across markdown headings.

reasons: The pin-29 quote matches the opinion text on slip op. 29 character-for-character apart from ordinary line wrapping.
The quoted passage directly supports the page's application point that the closed shoebox was not immediately incriminating and probable cause was lacking.
The words 'tiniest crack' appear in the opinion text on slip op. 31 in the passage rejecting the Commonwealth's crack-or-perforation theory.
The surrounding content-page quote tracks the disclosed opinion passage: the court said that theory would allow searches of any object with even the tiniest crack or perforation.
residual_risks: The lake pin stores only the text-fragment phrase, not the full quoted sentence used on the page.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Store the full quoted sentence for pin-31 if the page continues to quote the surrounding passage.
